summary: Tadeusz Skorupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of London in 1978 and served as Professor and Reader at SOAS University of London, with a research stay at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Tai-shing Wut specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998) and served as an Assistant Professor at the City University of Hong Kong from 2009 to 2014.
Taido Kitamura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held academic posts at Shuchiin University, including assistant professor (attested 1980) and a post attested from 1994 to 1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton, born in 1950, works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Columbia University and Graduate Theological Union (Ph.D.), he studied under multiple traditional teachers, taught at various institutions, and served at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994) and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010).

Taijun Inokuchi is a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts as lecturer and committee member at Ryukoku University (attested 1963, 1973–1987) and served as representative for The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue, he became an Indian philosophy professor at the University of Tokyo in 1912 and lectured at Komazawa and Japan Women's University.

Taiken Kyuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Vienna in 1999 and served as an Associate Professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hiroshima University. He held an assistant professorship at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, earning a PhD in 2016. He also served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2015).

Taikyo Tanigawa (born 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Koyasan University and Toyo University (Ph.D. 1994), he held positions at Koyasan University, including assistant professor (attested 1980–1988) and professor (attested 2005, 2026).
Taion Satomi (born 1909) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University until 1933. He served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).

Taira Shidehara (1870–1953) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1893 to 1896 and later held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1898–1900) and the University of Tokyo (~1900–1906).

Tairyo Makita (1912–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto Universities. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (1949–1976), taught at Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University, and was president of Saitama Institute of Technology (1997).
Tairyu Tsunoda (born 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and became a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

Taisei Iwata (born 1937) specializes in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Taisen Deshimaru (1914–1982) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Kodo Sawaki from circa 1936 to 1965 and founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, later serving as a professor at Komazawa University and concurrent lecturer at the Eastern Institute (both attested 1990).
Taishun Mibu (1913–1980) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Taisho University from circa 1934 to 1937 and later served as its library director from circa 1954 to 1980.

Taitetsu Unno (1929–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley and the University of Tokyo, and served as Jill Ker Conway Professor Emeritus of Religion at Smith College (1971–1998).

Taitsu Kono (born 1930) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University (~1948–1952) and under Mumon Yamada (~1952–1965). He later held a post at Hanazono University from circa 2000 to 2004.
